issues.description: Top-level class name and file structure in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java: the template declares a class named 'AnimalFarm' (and contains duplicated/nested class content and a misplaced 'package' statement inside a method), whereas the problem statement UML and the solution expect a top-level public class named 'Farm' with the methods and fields described. This mismatch causes a compilation error and prevents students from implementing or using the intended 'Farm' type (Main and tests expect a class named Farm with a List<Animal>, constructor, addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, and singFarmSong).
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the contents of src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java with a correct skeleton matching the specification: keep the single top-level 'package de.tum.cit.ase;' line, declare 'public class Farm' (not AnimalFarm), include a private List<Animal> animals field, a no-argument constructor that initializes animals = new ArrayList<>(), getter and setter for animals, and the methods addAnimal(Animal), feedAllAnimals(), singFarmSong(), and a private helper singFarmSongVerse(Animal). Remove any duplicated or nested class declarations and any 'package' statements inside method bodies so the file compiles and aligns with the UML and Main usage. Leaving TODO comments in method bodies is acceptable, but the file must compile and the class name/signature must match the problem and solution.

issues.description: The exercise requires a class named 'Farm' (problem statement UML and tests refer to Farm), but the template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares a public class named 'AnimalFarm'. The solution repository implements the class as 'Farm'. This naming mismatch (template: public class AnimalFarm vs expected 'Farm' and solution: 'Farm') prevents a clear mapping from requirements to starter code and will cause Java compilation errors because the public class name does not match the filename.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the public class in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java from 'AnimalFarm' to 'Farm' so the class name matches the filename and the problem statement. Ensure the class API (constructors, methods addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong, getters/setters for animals) matches the specification and the solution implementation.
